doc.title: Arturo Sandoval interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2023

title: Dizzy's 'funny notes' and learning tunes in the trumpet key
summary: Dizzy called odd notes 'funny notes'; Sandoval learns chords on piano in the trumpet key, discussed with 'My Funny Valentine', and says piano and trumpet inform each other.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: You know something funny, one day in one of my hundreds of conversations with my hero and mentor John Birks Gillespie, that’s his real name, because I never would agree with that nickname of Dizzy because he was anything but Dizzy. He was a really smart guy. He was a genius and creator of a complete different style of music. But I asked him, “Dizzy, please explain to me those weird notes that you play within the chord?” And he looked at me and said, “I don’t call that weird. I call it funny notes.” And I’m going to share with you another trick that I’ve been doing for many, many, many years. When I want to learn a specific tune I learn the chords first on the piano. But instead of playing in the piano one key down, I learn it in the trumpet key. That helps me as well. Because when I’m improvising I remember not only the chord but the notes that I was playing in the same key. I don’t have to transpose, you understand what I mean? It’s easier.
So you’re playing “My Funny Valentine” in D minor on the piano, so that when you go to play the trumpet you’re there?
Right but I mean normally that tune is in C minor I think so —
Oh you’re right, you’re right, yeah. Uh, I don’t know, [plays trumpet] you’re right. It’s C minor. But I learned it in D minor on the piano. Yes.
Does your trumpet playing end up sort of this reversal like do you do things on the trumpet and say oh, I should try that on the piano?
Oh absolutely. It’s a two way, it’s a two way thing of course. Your element — one thing — and the other one, you know, you have to, in the end, it’s a way to create your speech
